text: リュックを私のガードにしたいんですけど
translation: I'd like to make Rikku one of my guardians.

vocabulary.meaning: I was wondering if… / I'd like to… (soft request/explanation)

grammar: 〜んですけど is a softened request form — stating one's intention/wish and implicitly asking for approval, without directly commanding or demanding.

text: 顔を上げろ
translation: Raise your face. / Look up.
grammar: 〜ろ is the plain imperative form of a verb (上げる → 上げろ), used for direct commands, common among male speech.

text: 顔を見せろ / ああいいよ
translation: Show me your face. / Yeah, fine.

text: 目を開けろ
translation: Open your eyes.

text: やはりな
translation: Just as I thought.

vocabulary.meaning: as expected, just as I thought, sure enough

grammar: やはりな — the な at the end adds a contemplative, self-confirming nuance: Auron recognizing that Rikku is Al Bhed (her eyes give it away).

text: だ、だめ?
translation: I-is that bad? / Is it no good?
grammar: The repeated だ stutter (だ、だめ) conveys Rikku's nervousness.

text: 覚悟はいいのか
translation: Are you prepared for this?
grammar: 覚悟はいいのか — literally 'Is your resolve good/ready?' A set phrase asking whether someone is mentally prepared for hardship ahead.

text: たりまえです
translation: Of course!
grammar: たりまえ is a casual contraction of 当たり前 (あたりまえ), dropping the あた— in fast speech.

text: というわけで / いいんだよね
translation: So that's the deal. / That's okay, right?

vocabulary.meaning: so, that's how it is, for that reason
right? / that's the case, isn't it? (seeking confirmation)

grammar: というわけで wraps up a situation and transitions to a conclusion or action, similar to 'so then' in English.

text: ユーナが望むなら / 私はぜひ
translation: If that's what Yuna wants, / I'm all for it.

vocabulary.meaning: to wish, to desire, to hope for

text: リュックはいい子だよ / 俺も世話になったし
translation: Rikku's a good kid. / She's looked after me too.

vocabulary.meaning: to be taken care of by, to be indebted to someone's help

grammar: 〜し at the end adds a reason/supporting point, implying 'and that's one reason among others.'

text: そうだな / にぎやかになっていいかもな / そうそう
translation: Yeah, you're right. / It might be nice to have things livelier. / Exactly, exactly.

text: じゃあ / 私はにぎやか担当ってことで / 不思議だった
translation: Then / I'll be in charge of keeping things lively! / It was strange, though.

vocabulary.meaning: so it's settled that…, with that understanding

grammar: 〜ってことで signals a casual settlement of an arrangement: 'so that means I'm the lively one.'

text: ワッカは / あんなにアルベド族が嫌いなの
translation: Wakka hates the Al Bhed that much?
grammar: The sentence ends without a verb (ellipsis) — the の nominalizer turns it into a wondering question: 'Is it that he hates them that much?'

text: よろしくお願いします / リュックがアルベド族だって / 気づかなかった。
translation: Nice to meet you / I didn't realize Rikku was Al Bhed.

vocabulary.word: よろしくお願いします
vocabulary.reading: よろしくおねがいします
vocabulary.meaning: pleased to meet you / I'm in your care
to notice, to realize, to become aware

grammar: 〜だって here is a casual quotative/report particle: 'that Rikku is Al Bhed' — Rikku narrating her internal surprise.

text: お待ちしておりました、ユーナ様。
translation: We have been awaiting you, Lady Yuna.

vocabulary.meaning: to wait (humble form of 待つ)
was/have been (humble past of いる)

grammar: お待ちしておりました is a double-humble construction: お〜する (humble action) + おる (humble auxiliary). Extremely formal/deferential register.

text: ようこそ、グアドサラムへ。
translation: Welcome to Guadosalam.

text: ささ、ユーナ様、こちらへ。 / あ、あの…
translation: Now then, Lady Yuna, this way please. / Um, excuse me…

text: なんなんだ、あんた。 / あ、あ、これは失礼。
translation: Who do you think you are? / Oh, oh, excuse my rudeness.

vocabulary.meaning: what's the deal with you? / just who are you? (irritated question)

grammar: なんなんだ is an emphatic doubled form of なんだ, expressing frustration or challenge.

text: 私トアメルグワドと申します
translation: I am called Tromell Guado.

vocabulary.meaning: to say, to be called (humble form of 言う/名乗る)

grammar: 〜と申します is the humble self-introduction form: 'I humbly call myself…' Used in formal contexts.

text: グワドの族長シーボアグワドの身内の者でございます
translation: I am a member of the household of Jyscal Guado, leader of the Guado.

vocabulary.meaning: one's household, family members, close associates

grammar: でございます is the most formal level of the copula, used in very polite/formal speech or service contexts.

text: シーモア様がユーナ様に大切なお話があるそうで
translation: It seems Lord Seymour has an important matter to discuss with Lady Yuna.

vocabulary.meaning: it seems that…, I hear that… (hearsay)

grammar: 〜があるそうで: そうで (from そうだ, hearsay) is left open/trailing, softening the statement and implying a polite transition to action.

text: 私にですか?どんなお話でしょう?
translation: With me? What kind of matter might it be?

vocabulary.meaning: what kind of, what sort of

text: どうあれまずはシーモア様のお屋敷へどうぞ / もちろん皆様も歓迎いたしますよ
translation: Whatever the case, please first come to Lord Seymour's manor. / Of course, everyone is welcome.

vocabulary.meaning: whatever the case may be, regardless

grammar: 歓迎いたします — いたす is the humble form of する, appropriate for a host addressing guests.

text: シーモア様をお呼びしてまいります / しばしお待ちを
translation: I will go and call Lord Seymour. / Please wait just a moment.

vocabulary.meaning: to call/summon (humble form of 呼ぶ)
go/come (humble form of 行く/来る)

grammar: お呼びしてまいります is doubly humble: お〜する (humble action verb) + まいる (humble movement). Very deferential register.

text: ほっほっほっ、お客人を迎えるのは楽しいものです。
translation: Ho ho ho, welcoming guests is such a pleasure.

vocabulary.meaning: it is something that…, it is indeed the case that… (emphatic/reflective)

grammar: 〜ものです adds a reflective, general-truth nuance: 'welcoming guests is just such a pleasant thing.'

text: ジスカル様が亡くなって以来、この屋敷は静かすぎました。
translation: Ever since Lord Jyscal passed away, this manor has been far too quiet.

vocabulary.meaning: to pass away, to die (polite euphemism)

text: ジスカル老子の死は、スピラにとって大きな損失です。 / ジスカル老子って、そんなにすごいのか?
translation: The death of Grand Maester Jyscal is a great loss for Spira. / Was Grand Maester Jyscal really that amazing?

text: グアド族にエボンの教えを広めたんだ。まったく、教え方をなくした。
translation: He spread Yevon's teachings to the Guado. Truly, we've lost a great teacher.

vocabulary.meaning: to spread, to propagate, to popularize
way of teaching, manner of teaching

grammar: 教え方をなくした — literally 'lost a way of teaching'; in context means the world has lost a masterful teacher.

text: そう、まことに残念です。
translation: Yes, it is truly regrettable.

text: しかし、我らには新たな指導者、シーモア様がおられる。 / シーモア様はグワードと人の間に生まれたお方
translation: However, we have a new leader — Lord Seymour. / Lord Seymour is one born between the Guado and humans.
grammar: おられる is the respectful (尊敬語) form of いる, used when referring to someone of high status.

text: 必ずや二つの種族を結ぶ絆となってくださいます
translation: He will surely become the bond that unites the two races.

vocabulary.meaning: surely, without doubt, certainly (emphatic literary form)
to bind, to tie, to connect

grammar: 必ずや is a literary/formal intensifier of 必ず, common in elevated speech.

text: いいえそれだけではありません / シーモア様はこのスピラに生きるすべてのものの / 未来を照らす光となるでしょうな
translation: No, that is not all. / Lord Seymour will become the light that illuminates the future of all living things in Spira.

vocabulary.meaning: will probably be, indeed will be (conjecture with agreement-seeking な)

text: それぐらいにしておけトアメル / あまり持ち上げられると居心地が悪い
translation: That's enough, Tromell. / Being flattered too much makes me uncomfortable.

vocabulary.word: それぐらいにしておく
vocabulary.reading: それぐらいにしておく
vocabulary.meaning: to leave it at that, to stop there
to flatter, to praise excessively; to lift up
comfort, how comfortable one feels (in a place/situation)

grammar: 持ち上げられると — passive + conditional と: 'when/if I am flattered.' The passive indicates Seymour is on the receiving end of the praise.

text: ようこそ皆さん
translation: Welcome, everyone.

text: あのお話って
translation: About that matter…
grammar: 〜って is a casual topic marker/quotative, here used to raise a subject: 'about that thing you mentioned…'

text: そう結論を急がずにごゆるりと / ユーナは先を急ぐみだ手短に済ませてもらいたい
translation: Now now, don't rush to conclusions — take your time. / Yuna is in a hurry to move on, so I'd like to keep this brief.

vocabulary.meaning: at your leisure, slowly and comfortably (formal/archaic)
to be in a hurry to move forward, to rush ahead
to finish, to wrap up, to get through
I want you to do… (requesting a favor)

grammar: 急がずに — negative て-form of 急ぐ using ず (classical negative), equivalent to 急がないで.

text: しっけい久方ぶりに客人を迎えたので / ついユーナ殿こちらへ
translation: Forgive me — it's been quite a while since I've had guests, so I got carried away. / Lady Yuna, this way please.

vocabulary.meaning: after a long time, after quite a while (literary)
unintentionally, inadvertently, before one knows it

grammar: 久方ぶりに is a more literary variant of 久しぶりに, conveying 'after a considerable time.'

text: そう、ザナルカンド / およそ1000年前の姿です
translation: Yes — Zanarkand. This is its appearance from about 1000 years ago.

text: 半永を極めた機械仕掛けの町ザナルカンド
translation: Zanarkand — a mechanized city that reached the pinnacle of civilization.

vocabulary.meaning: to master, to reach the extreme of, to attain the peak of

text: 彼女はここで暮らしました
translation: She lived here.

vocabulary.meaning: to live, to reside, to spend one's days

text: 彼女?
translation: She?

text: 歴史上初めてシンを倒し世界を救ったお方です
translation: She is the one who first defeated Sin in history and saved the world.

text: そしてあなたはその名を受け継いでいる / 父がつけてくれたそうです
translation: And you have inherited that name. / It seems your father gave it to you.

vocabulary.meaning: to inherit, to succeed to, to carry on
to do for one's benefit (someone does something for you)
I hear that…, it seems that… (hearsay)

text: ブラスカ様はあなたに願いを託したのでしょう
translation: Lord Braska must have entrusted his wish to you.

vocabulary.meaning: to entrust, to leave in someone's care
I suppose that…, it must be that… (polite conjecture)

text: ユーナレスカ様のごとく真に立ち向かえと
translation: To truly face it, just as Lady Yunalesca did.

vocabulary.meaning: just like, in the manner of (formal/literary)
to confront, to face up to, to stand up against

grammar: 〜のごとく is a literary comparative: 'in the same way as Yunalesca.' The sentence ends with と, a quotative particle indicating Seymour is paraphrasing Braska's implied wish.

text: しかしユーナレスカ様はお一人で世界を救ったのではありません
translation: However, Lady Yunalesca did not save the world alone.

vocabulary.meaning: it is not the case that… (polite negation of a nominalized clause)

text: 無敵の真を倒したのは / 二つの心を固く結んだ
translation: What defeated the invincible Sin was / two hearts bound firmly together —

vocabulary.meaning: to bind, to tie, to connect

grammar: 倒したのは — the nominalizer の turns 倒した into a noun clause: 'the thing/one that defeated.' Sets up a contrastive は topic.

text: 永遠に変わらぬ愛の絆
translation: The eternal, unchanging bond of love.

vocabulary.meaning: classical negative (does not ~); attributive form of ない

grammar: 変わらぬ is the classical/literary negative attributive form of 変わる (≒ 変わらない), used in formal or poetic contexts.

text: 我
translation: I…
grammar: 我 (われ) is an archaic/formal first-person pronoun. Seymour uses it to begin his marriage proposal, cut off before completion.

text: うわぁ顔真っ赤 / 大丈夫か
translation: Wow, your face is bright red! / Are you okay?

text: 結婚を申し込まれました
translation: I was proposed to. / I received a marriage proposal.

vocabulary.meaning: to propose, to apply, to make an offer

grammar: 申し込まれました — passive of 申し込む: 'was proposed to,' showing the action was done to Yuna (by Seymour).

text: マジっすか
translation: Are you serious?!

vocabulary.meaning: is it? / really? (casual polite question, contraction of ですか)

grammar: 〜っす is a casual contraction of 〜です, used in relaxed/informal polite speech.

text: ユーナの使命を知っているはずだが / もちろんユーナ殿の
translation: You must know Yuna's mission. / Of course I do — it is Lady Yuna's mission.

vocabulary.meaning: should be, must be, expected to be

grammar: 〜はずだ expresses a reasoned expectation: 'it should be the case that you know.' Auron is making a pointed challenge.

text: いや召喚師の使命はスピラに平和と安定をもたらすこと
translation: No — a summoner's mission is to bring peace and stability to Spira.

vocabulary.meaning: to bring about, to cause, to bring (a result)

grammar: 〜こと at the end nominalizes the clause: 'the thing that is [the mission]' — a common pattern for defining something.

text: しかしシンを倒すことだけが全てではありますまい / シンに苦しむ民の心を少しでも晴れやかに
translation: But defeating Sin alone is not everything. / Even a little brightness for the hearts of the people who suffer under Sin —

vocabulary.meaning: surely is not…, cannot be… (formal negative conjecture)
to suffer, to be in pain
even a little, at least a little

grammar: ありますまい is a formal/archaic negative conjecture form (≒ ないでしょう). More elevated register than everyday speech.

text: それもまた民を導く者の務め / 私はエボンの老子としてユーナ殿に結婚を申し込んだのです
translation: That too is the duty of one who leads the people. / I proposed to Lady Yuna in my capacity as a Grand Maester of Yevon.

vocabulary.meaning: as (in the capacity of), in the role of
to propose, to make an offer (humble form of 言う in compounds)

grammar: 〜のです (〜のだ) at the sentence end provides an explanatory/emphatic nuance — Seymour is justifying and explaining his proposal.

text: スピラは劇場ではない / ひとときの夢で観客を酔わせても現実は変わる
translation: Spira is not a theater. / Even if you intoxicate the audience with a fleeting dream, reality does not change.

vocabulary.meaning: fleeting, momentary, of a brief time
to intoxicate, to enchant, to make (someone) drunk (causative of 酔う)

grammar: 〜ても is the concessive form: 'even if you do X, Y still happens.' Auron is countering Seymour's political romanticism.

text: それでも舞台に立つのが役者の務
translation: Even so, it is an actor's duty to take the stage.

vocabulary.meaning: to stand; to take the stage

grammar: 〜のが is a nominalizing pattern: 'the thing of standing on stage' = 'standing on stage' (subject of the sentence). Seymour deflects Auron's criticism with poetic flair.

text: 今すぐに答える必要はありません / どうかじっくり考えてください
translation: You don't need to answer right now. / Please take your time and think it over carefully.

text: そうさせてもらおう / 出るぞ / ユーナ殿
translation: I'll take you up on that. / We're leaving. / Lady Yuna.

vocabulary.meaning: to take the liberty of doing so, to accept that offer (polite self-permission)

grammar: 〜させてもらう is a polite expression meaning 'I'll take the liberty of doing X,' often used to accept an offer graciously.

text: 良い返事をお待ちしています
translation: I await your favorable reply.

vocabulary.meaning: to wait (humble form of 待つ)

text: 何のために留まっているのです
translation: For what reason are you still here?

vocabulary.meaning: for what purpose, for what reason
to remain, to stay, to linger

grammar: 〜のです (〜のだ) adds an explanatory/interrogative tone, demanding a reason — Tromell is challenging why Tidus/others are still lingering.

text: これは失礼 / 我々グアドは異界の匂いに敏感なもので
translation: Pardon me. / We Guado are sensitive to the scent of the Farplane, you see.

vocabulary.meaning: the Farplane, the otherworld, the realm of the dead
because it is (such a thing); you see, it's because… (explanatory)

grammar: 〜なもので is an explanatory/apologetic phrase meaning 'it's because [we are such beings],' softening the observation.

text: 大将冠士の娘ユーナと / グアドの族長シーマは
translation: Yuna, daughter of High Summoner Braska, and / Seymour, leader of the Guado —

vocabulary.meaning: High Summoner (title for a summoner who defeated Sin)

text: その二人がエボンの名の下 / 種族の壁を越えて結婚か
translation: Those two, under the name of Yevon, / crossing the barrier of race to wed — is that it?

vocabulary.meaning: under the name of, in the name of
to cross, to overcome, to transcend

grammar: Sentence ends with か, a question/rhetorical marker expressing the speaker's pondering: 'So that's the picture, is it?'

text: 確かにスピラにとって明るい話題になるわね / でもよ、ほんとひとときの夢って感じだよな
translation: It certainly would be a bright topic for Spira. / But really, it feels just like a fleeting dream, doesn't it.

vocabulary.meaning: it feels like…, it has the sense of…

grammar: わね — feminine sentence-final particle combining わ (mild assertion) and ね (seeking agreement). よな — masculine seeking agreement at the end of the second speaker's line.

text: ていうかさ、早く旅の続き行かない?
translation: I mean, shouldn't we just hurry up and get back to the journey?

vocabulary.meaning: I mean, or rather, more to the point (conversation redirect)
isn't it? / don't you want to? (inviting agreement or action)

text: 冗談きついっすよ / ああ、やきもち?
translation: That's a bit much! / Ah, are you jealous?

vocabulary.meaning: harsh, severe, heavy; here: 'a bit much'

grammar: 冗談きつい — shortened/casual form of 冗談がきつい: 'the joke/situation is too harsh.' Often means 'you're too much' or 'no way.'

text: 違うって、シンを倒すのが一番 / それ以外は後回しだろ?
translation: That's not it! Defeating Sin is the top priority. / Everything else comes second, right?

vocabulary.meaning: to be wrong, to differ; 'no, that's not it'
putting off, leaving for later, lower priority

grammar: 〜って after 違う emphasizes the denial: 'I'm telling you, that's not it!' Colloquial assertive use of って.

text: 余計なことに巻き込まれちまったよな / 余計なことなのかな / マジっすか
translation: We've gotten wrapped up in something unnecessary, huh. / Is it really unnecessary? / Seriously?

vocabulary.meaning: to get dragged/wrapped into, to become involved in
ended up doing (casual contraction of 〜てしまった)
I wonder if it is… (gentle self-questioning)

grammar: 〜ちまった is a contracted form of 〜てしまった, used in casual male speech: 'ended up [doing something, often regrettably].'

text: 私が結婚することでスピラジュンの人たちが少しでも明るい気持ちになれたら / そんな風に役に立てたらそれも素敵だなって思うんだ
translation: If my getting married could make even a few people across Spira feel even a little brighter — / if I could be useful in that way, I think that would be wonderful too.

vocabulary.meaning: to be useful, to be of service

grammar: 〜なって思うんだ — casual thought-reporting: 'I find myself thinking that it would be…' The んだ adds a personal, reflective nuance.

text: こういうことって今まで想像したことなかった
translation: I had never imagined anything like this until now.

vocabulary.meaning: this kind of thing, something like this
until now, up to this point

grammar: 〜したことなかった — experience + negation: 'had never done X before.' The topic marker って makes it casual and reflective.

text: だからよく考えてから返事をしたいの / マジっすか / 結婚して旅をやめちゃうのもありだと思うな
translation: So I want to think it over carefully before giving my answer. / Seriously? / I think stopping the journey to get married could also be an option.

vocabulary.meaning: to think carefully, to think it through
that option is also possible, that could also work (casual)

grammar: 〜のもありだと思う — ありだ means 'it's a valid option/possibility,' colloquial expression for something being acceptable or on the table.

text: 旅は続けるよ / シーモア様もきっとわかってくれると思うな
translation: I'll continue the journey. / I'm sure Lord Seymour will understand.

vocabulary.meaning: to understand (doing it for one's benefit)

text: そうだね / 私召喚師だもん
translation: That's right. / I am a summoner, after all.

vocabulary.meaning: because…, after all (casual/childlike reason-giving, variant of だもの)

grammar: だもん is a casual, slightly childlike form of だもの (だから), giving a reason with a soft, personal tone. Characteristic of Yuna's speech.

text: シンを倒すって決めたんだから / ブラスカと同じようにな
translation: Because I've decided to defeat Sin — / just like Braska.

vocabulary.meaning: in the same way, just like

text: それなら何を考える必要があるスタ / って叫びたかった
translation: Then what is there to think about! / is what I wanted to shout.

vocabulary.meaning: to shout, to cry out, to yell
wanted to do (past tense of たい)

grammar: 〜って叫びたかった — って is a quotative particle: 'I wanted to shout [that].' Tidus narrating an internal impulse he held back.

text: 私、異界に行ってくる / 異界で父さんに会って考えてみるね / そうね、気が済むまで考えなさい
translation: I'm going to go to the Farplane. / I'll meet my father there and think things over. / All right, think it through until you're satisfied.

vocabulary.meaning: the Farplane (realm of the dead in FFX)
to go and do (then return); indicates going somewhere to do something
to feel satisfied, to feel at peace, to be done with
think (gentle imperative, often from someone older/senior)

grammar: 〜てくる here is a movement pattern: 'go and do X (and come back).' 気が済むまで = 'until you feel satisfied/resolved.'

text: 誰もユーナに聞かなかったのが不思議だった
translation: It was strange that no one asked Yuna.
grammar: 〜のが不思議だった — の nominalizes the clause, making it the subject: 'the fact that no one asked was strange.'

text: シーモアのこと、好きなのか、って
translation: Whether she likes Seymour — that question.
grammar: 〜って here is a quotative: Tidus is citing the question he (and no one else) thought to ask. The sentence trails off, leaving the question hanging.

text: 質問っす / 異界のことなんだけどさ / 誰かが死んだら
translation: I have a question. / It's about the Farplane — / when someone dies,
grammar: 〜んだけどさ — の+だ+けど+さ: a very casual way to introduce a topic, like 'so the thing is…'

text: 召喚師が異界送りするんだろ / んで死んじゃった人の魂は
translation: A summoner sends them to the Farplane, right? / And then the soul of the person who died —

vocabulary.meaning: sending to the Farplane (the Sending, the ritual performed by summoners)
and then, so (casual, contracted form of それで)

text: 異界に行くんだよな / でさこれから行くのが / その異界 / そこには、ユーナの親父さんがいる。 / 要するに、死んじゃった人が住んでるのか?
translation: goes to the Farplane, right? / And the Farplane is where we're about to go. / That's where Yuna's father is. / In other words, is it where dead people live?

vocabulary.meaning: from now on, from here, about to
in other words, to sum up, in short
to live, to reside, to dwell

text: まあ、変なこと考えてるんだろ。
translation: Well, you're thinking some weird things, aren't you.

text: まあ、行けばわかるさ。
translation: Well, you'll understand once you go.

vocabulary.meaning: sentence-final particle giving light reassurance or slight dismissal

grammar: 〜ばわかる — conditional: 'if you go, you'll understand.' The さ particle adds a casual, reassuring or slightly dismissive nuance.

text: どうして行かないんだ? / ふん… / 異界は気に食わん
translation: Why aren't you going? / Hmph… / The Farplane doesn't sit well with me.

vocabulary.meaning: to not like, to be displeased with, to rub one wrong

grammar: 気に食わん — 食わん is the classical/dialectal negative of 食う, equivalent to 食わない. Kimahri's blunt, archaic speech style.

text: あ?はぁ… / 怖いんだろ? / 未来の道を決めるために過去の力を借りる
translation: Huh? Hah… / You're just scared, aren't you? / To decide the path forward, we borrow the strength of the past.

text: 異界とはそんな場所だ / ショーニアはさっさと行け
translation: That is what the Farplane is. / Get moving already.
grammar: 〜とは is a formal/definitive topic marker used when defining or explaining something: 'As for what X is…'

text: 本当はさ、死人じゃなくて思い出に会いに行く場所なんだよ
translation: The truth is, it's not a place to meet the dead — it's a place to meet your memories.

vocabulary.meaning: the truth is, actually, in reality

grammar: 〜なんだよ — explanatory のだ: Rikku is explaining the true nature of the Farplane with an informative, 'let me tell you' tone.

text: 会いたいって思う気持ちに原稿虫が反応するの
translation: The pyreflies react to your feelings of wanting to meet someone.

vocabulary.meaning: pyreflies (FFX term; lit. 'manuscript bugs' — spirit particles)

grammar: 〜って思う気持ち — embedded quotative: 'the feeling of thinking/wanting to meet.' の at end is feminine explanatory ending.

text: でね、原稿虫が人の形になる / 要するに幻ってわけ
translation: And then the pyreflies take the form of a person. / In short, it's an illusion.

vocabulary.meaning: that means, that's the reason (casual explanatory conclusion)

grammar: 〜ってわけ is a casual feminine concluding expression: 'which means, in short, it's X.' Similar to というわけ but more casual.

text: ふーん / じゃあ、行ってらっしゃい / あれ?お前行かないのか? / 思い出は心の中に
translation: Hmm. / Well then, off you go. / Huh? Aren't you going? / My memories are in my heart.

vocabulary.meaning: have a good trip, see you later (farewell to someone leaving)
inside one's heart, within the heart

grammar: 行ってらっしゃい is a set phrase combining 行って (te-form of 行く) + いらっしゃい (respectful imperative of いる/来る): 'go and come back safely.'

text: 思い出は優しいから甘えちゃダメなの
translation: Memories are kind, so you mustn't depend on them.

vocabulary.meaning: to depend on, to be spoiled by, to lean on emotionally
you mustn't do… (casual prohibition, 〜てはダメ)

grammar: 甘えちゃダメ = 甘えてはダメ: 'mustn't lean on them.' Rikku's reasoning for not going — she keeps her memories private and sacred.

text: なんだ?
translation: What?

vocabulary.meaning: what is it? what's this? (casual surprise/question)

text: 初めて来た異界のことより
translation: More than the Farplane I was visiting for the first time,
grammar: 〜より sets up a contrast: 'more than [the Farplane itself]…' — leading into what Tidus was actually preoccupied with.

text: ユーナの気持ちが気になってた / ユーナの両親って仲良さそうでさ
translation: I was worried about Yuna's feelings. / Yuna's parents seemed like they got along well,

vocabulary.meaning: to be concerned about, to have on one's mind
on good terms, close (as a couple/friends)

text: そんなの見たらユーナの気持ちも結婚する方に傾くかも
translation: If she saw that, her feelings might lean toward marriage.

vocabulary.meaning: to lean, to tilt, to incline toward
might, maybe (casual form of かもしれない)

grammar: 〜たら with 見る: 'if she were to see that.' The conditional sets up a worrying possibility in Tidus's mind.

text: とかさ
translation: …or something like that.
grammar: とかさ trails off as if listing or hedging — 'stuff like that, you know.' Used to soften or understate what was just said.

text: すぐお前に会いに来るつもりだったけど
translation: I had intended to come see you right away, but…

vocabulary.meaning: had intended to, was planning to (unfulfilled intention)

grammar: 〜つもりだったけど — past tense of 〜つもり: 'I intended to, but [something got in the way].' The けど trails off, implying regret.

text: すまん / これからシャキッとすっから勘弁してくれ
translation: Sorry. / From now on I'll shape up, so forgive me.

vocabulary.meaning: sorry, I'm sorry (rough/masculine form of 済まない)
to pull oneself together, to snap to it, to straighten up
to forgive, to pardon, to let it slide

grammar: すっから — casual contraction of するから: 'because I will [shape up].' Wakka speaking informally to his brother Chappu's spirit.

text: ブリッツボールも引退したし / あとはガード一筋だ
translation: I've retired from blitzball too, / and from here on I'm devoted solely to being a guardian.

vocabulary.meaning: single-mindedly, devoted to one thing only

grammar: ガード一筋だ — 一筋 means 'one track, single-mindedly committed.' A common expression for total devotion to a single path.

text: お前になんとなく似てる奴が現れてな
translation: A guy who somehow reminds me of you showed up, you see.
grammar: 〜てな — te-form + な (sentence-final): 'and so…' or 'you see, the thing is…' Wakka trails off, transitioning to the next thought.

text: そいつと一緒に旅をしてるうちに思った
translation: While travelling together with him, I started to think —

vocabulary.meaning: while doing…, in the course of doing…

grammar: 〜うちに indicates that something happened or changed during the course of an ongoing action: 'while I was travelling with him, I started to think…'

text: お前もどこかで生きてるんじゃないかってな
translation: That maybe you were alive somewhere out there.
grammar: 〜んじゃないかってな — embedded speculation with quotative って and softening な: Wakka half-wishing, half-wondering if Chappu might still be alive.

text: でもやっぱりお前は異界の住人なんだよな
translation: But after all, you're a resident of the Farplane now.

vocabulary.meaning: as expected, after all, sure enough

grammar: 〜なんだよな — なんだ (explanatory) + よ (affirmation) + な (reflective agreement-seeking): a gentle, resigned confirmation of something sad.

text: はっきりわかったよ
translation: That became perfectly clear to me.

text: そっちはどうだ / なあさっき話した奴にな
translation: How are things on your side? / Hey, that guy I was just talking about —

vocabulary.meaning: that side, over there, your side (casual)

text: お前の剣をやったんだ / いいよね
translation: I gave him your sword. / That's okay, right?

vocabulary.meaning: to give (casual; gives from speaker downward or to peer)

grammar: やったんだ — past of やる + んだ (explanatory): 'I went and gave him [the sword],' with a slight confessional nuance, hence 'いいよね?' (that's okay, right?).

text: 彼は死んで 私は生きている
translation: He is dead, and I am alive.
grammar: Simple juxtaposition: 〜て connects two contrasting states. The starkness reflects Lulu's confrontation with loss.

text: ここに来るとよくわかるわね / そろそろ私も人生前向きに考えないとね
translation: Coming here makes it very clear. / It's about time I started thinking about my own life in a more forward-looking way.

vocabulary.meaning: I should…, I need to… (mild obligation with softening ね)

grammar: 〜ないとね — shortened from 〜なければならない: 'I really should/must,' with ね softening it into a gentle self-reminder.

text: な、何? / 前向きって何よ? / てめえ
translation: Wh-what? / What do you mean 'forward-looking'?! / You!

vocabulary.meaning: what is that! / what do you mean! (feminine, irritated)
you (very rough, insulting; used in anger)

grammar: 何よ — feminine/emotional form of なんだ, expressing indignation. てめえ is a rough/hostile pronoun, here expressing Wakka's outrage.

text: チャップのことにこだわらないってことじゃないの? / チャップには悪いけど、新しい誰かと付き合うとか
translation: Doesn't it mean not clinging to Chappu? / Sorry to Chappu, but like dating someone new…

vocabulary.meaning: to be particular about, to cling to, to be hung up on
doesn't that mean…? / isn't that what it means?
bad; here: 'sorry' (〜には悪いけど = sorry to, but)
to date, to go out with; also to associate with

grammar: 〜には悪いけど is a set expression of apology: 'I feel bad for X, but…'

text: なるほど、そういうのもありね / ふーん、輪っかと付き合うとか / どうして輪っかが出てくるのよ
translation: I see, that could also be an option. / Hmm — like dating Wakka? / Why does Wakka come up?

vocabulary.meaning: I see, I understand, that makes sense
that kind of thing is also possible/an option
to come out, to appear, to pop up

text: だって仲いいだろ / 仲がいいのとそういうことは全然別ね
translation: Well, you two get along so well. / Being close and that sort of thing are completely different.

vocabulary.meaning: but, because, after all (casual reason/mild protest)
to get along well, to be close

grammar: 〜のと〜は別 — 'X and Y are separate things' — contrasting two items using のと (connecting two nominalized clauses) + は (topic/contrast).

text: ああ、そうなの / そう、覚えておきなさい、少年
translation: Oh, is that so? / Yes — remember that, boy.

vocabulary.meaning: to keep in mind, to remember for future reference

grammar: 〜ておきなさい — ておく (do and keep it done/in mind) + なさい (gentle imperative): 'make sure to remember that.'

text: 女の子の気持ちを勘違いして恥かかないようなね
translation: So you don't misread a girl's feelings and embarrass yourself.

vocabulary.meaning: to embarrass oneself, to lose face
so as not to, in order to avoid…

grammar: 〜ないようにね — 'so that you don't…, okay?' The ね softens it into friendly advice.

text: え、覚えたく / 私も忘れないようにするわ / さよならチャップ
translation: Uh, noted. / I'll make sure not to forget either. / Goodbye, Chappu.

vocabulary.meaning: to make sure not to, to try not to

text: いつも不機嫌そうだってあんたは言ってたけど
translation: You always used to say I looked unhappy,

vocabulary.meaning: in a bad mood, sulky, unhappy

grammar: 〜だってあんたは言ってたけど — 'you used to say that…, but.' だって is quotative here; the けど trails into unspoken resolution.

text: 楽しかったよ
translation: It was fun.

text: とてもね
translation: Very much so.
grammar: とてもね — a sentence fragment emphasizing the previous statement. The ね adds quiet emotional resonance.

text: で、どう? / 決めたよ
translation: So, how is it? / I've decided.

text: そ、そりゃよかった / で、どっち?
translation: Oh, th-that's great! / So, which way?

vocabulary.meaning: that's great, that's a relief (casual relief expression)

grammar: そりゃ is a contraction of それは. The stutter (そ、そりゃ) shows Tidus trying to contain his eagerness.

text: 10年前 / 父さんがシンを倒した時のこと / 思い出したのね
translation: Ten years ago — / when Father defeated Sin — / I remembered that.
grammar: 〜のね — feminine sentence-final の + ね: gentle explanatory/shared-understanding tone. Yuna begins explaining her decision.

text: 私はベベルにいたんだけど / 街中が大騒ぎだった / みんな笑っていて
translation: I was in Bevelle at the time, / and the whole city was in an uproar. / Everyone was smiling,

vocabulary.meaning: throughout the city, the whole town

text: とっても楽しそうだった / シンを倒すのが
translation: They all looked so happy. / Defeating Sin —

vocabulary.meaning: very, so (casual form of とても)

text: 一番の明るい話題 / だよね
translation: is the greatest bright topic there is. / Right?

text: あれもこれもなんて / 欲張っちゃダメだよね
translation: I mustn't be greedy and want this and that too, right?

vocabulary.meaning: this and that, everything (wanting too much)
to be greedy, to want too much

grammar: 欲張っちゃダメ = 欲張ってはダメ: 'shouldn't be greedy.' The だよね seeks gentle agreement/confirmation.

text: じゃあ戻る / シーモアに返事するんだろ
translation: Then let's head back. / You're going to give Seymour your answer, right?

text: その前に / ジェクトさん / 呼んでみない?
translation: Before that — / Jecht. / Want to try calling for him?
grammar: 〜てみない? — negative form used as casual invitation: 'won't you try?' = 'want to try?'

text: 大丈夫、きっと来ないから / 思わないようにするのは、思うのと同じことなわけで
translation: It's okay — he definitely won't come. / Trying not to think about someone is the same as thinking about them.

vocabulary.reading: おもわないようにする
vocabulary.meaning: to try not to think about

grammar: 〜なわけで is an explanatory connective: Yuna explaining a subtle emotional truth about why she wanted Tidus to try calling Jecht.

text: ほら、来ない / 親父は死んだから、ここには来ないってことか
translation: See, he didn't come. / So does that mean Dad is dead, and that's why he can't come here?

vocabulary.meaning: see! look! (drawing attention to something proven)
so that means…? / does that mean…? (casual conclusion)

text: きっと、どこかで会えるんだよ / でも本当に親父が死んだったら、俺は、ユーナやスピラの人たちになんて謝れば
translation: I'm sure you'll meet him somewhere. / But if Dad is truly dead, how could I even apologize to Yuna and the people of Spira —
grammar: なんて謝れば — rhetorical: 'how could I possibly apologize?' The sentence trails without completing, showing Tidus's anguish.

text: いや、どうして俺があいつの代わりに謝るんだよ
translation: No wait — why should I be the one to apologize on his behalf?

vocabulary.meaning: in place of, on behalf of, instead of

text: 最低だな、親父 / ねえ、どうしてそんなに嫌いなの?
translation: You're the worst, Dad. / Hey, why do you hate him so much?

text: いちいち腹が立つんだよな、あいつ / あいつのせいで、俺と母さんは…
translation: He makes me angry about every little thing. / Because of him, Mom and I…

vocabulary.meaning: every single time, one by one, about every little thing
to get angry, to be irritated
because of (negative cause), due to, thanks to (blame)

grammar: 〜のせいで indicates blame: 'because of him [something bad happened].' The sentence cuts off with ellipsis (…), a moment of painful emotion.

text: 母さん…
translation: Mom…
grammar: A single word trailing off — Tidus sees his mother's image appear in the Farplane pyreflies.

text: 出てきちゃった / 綺麗な人だね
translation: She appeared. / She's a beautiful person.

vocabulary.meaning: ended up (doing), unexpectedly happened (casual 〜てしまった)

text: あれ?
translation: Huh?

vocabulary.meaning: huh? (exclamation of mild surprise or confusion)

text: 母さんは、異界送りなんてされなかったのに / 生きてる時から、死を受け入れていたんだよ
translation: Mom never even had the Sending performed for her, / yet she had already accepted death while she was still alive.

vocabulary.meaning: even though, despite the fact that (unexpected contrast)

grammar: 〜のに expresses contrast or surprise: 'even though she never had the Sending, she appears here.' The explanation follows — she had already accepted death inwardly.

text: ひどいな、それ / 俺いたのにな
translation: That's awful. / Even though I was there.
grammar: 俺いたのにな — 'even though I was there (she chose death over living for me).' のに expresses grievance; な adds a reflective, pained tone.

text: ごめん
translation: I'm sorry.

text: いいんだ / ああ、なんか俺
translation: It's okay. / Ah, somehow I…
grammar: いいんだ — the んだ makes this more self-directed: 'I'm telling myself it's fine.' なんか俺 trails off, building suspense before the realization.

text: わかっちゃった 何
translation: I just understood something. / What?

vocabulary.meaning: ended up (realizing); unexpectedly came to understand

grammar: わかっちゃった — the ちゃった (てしまった) here conveys a sudden, perhaps unwanted realization: 'it hit me, I finally understood.'

text: 親父が嫌いな理由
translation: The reason I hate Dad.
grammar: A bare noun phrase completing the previous sentence: 'what I realized was — the reason I hate Dad.'

text: なそんで俺ははっきり言ってやったんだ
translation: And so I said it clearly.

vocabulary.meaning: to tell someone off, to say (to them) forcefully (〜てやる = do for/against someone)

grammar: 言ってやった — 〜てやる indicates the speaker did something defiantly or assertively toward another: 'I went ahead and told him/her off.'

text: 本当 足りめいだろ / ああそうだけど
translation: It's true — he's the worst, isn't he? / Yeah, but…

vocabulary.meaning: lacking, not enough; here slang: 'the worst, terrible'

text: お母さん ちょっと待っててね / 親父がいると、母さんは俺の方を見てくれなかった
translation: Mom, wait just a moment. / When Dad was around, Mom never looked my way.

vocabulary.meaning: wait just a moment (casual, te-form of 待つ + いる contracted)
to look toward, to turn one's attention to
did not do for (one's benefit) — expressing a grievance

grammar: 〜てくれなかった — the くれる benefactive + past negative: 'she didn't do [that] for me,' carrying a sense of hurt.

text: だから俺は、親父が嫌いになっていったんだろうな
translation: So that's probably why I came to hate Dad.

vocabulary.meaning: to come to dislike, to grow to hate
to gradually do, to keep doing (progressive change away)
I suppose that's why… / must have been that… (self-reflective conjecture)

grammar: 嫌いになっていったんだろうな — a layered construction: 嫌いになる (come to hate) + 〜ていく (gradual change) + んだろうな (reflective conjecture). Tidus piecing together his own psychology.

text: 親父がいなくなってからさ、母さんはどんどん元気がなくなって
translation: And after Dad was gone, Mom just kept getting weaker and weaker,

vocabulary.meaning: to be gone, to disappear, to no longer be there
to lose energy/vitality, to become weaker

grammar: 〜てからさ — after + casual さ (pause filler). 〜てくる or 〜ていく shows progressive change over time.

text: 具合はどうだ? / あんたには関係ないだろ
translation: How are you feeling? / That's none of your business.

vocabulary.meaning: condition, state; how one is feeling (health)
has nothing to do with, irrelevant, none of one's business

text: あの人に死なれては、俺も困るのでな / 母さんが死ぬって言えな
translation: If that woman were to die, it would trouble me too. / He was saying Mom was going to die.

vocabulary.meaning: passive of 死ぬ: to suffer the death of someone (adversative passive)
to be troubled, to be in a fix

grammar: 死なれては — adversative passive (迷惑の受身): 'if she were to die [on me/to my detriment].' The は adds a conditional nuance of inconvenience.

text: 悪かった / 近所のおばさんが言ってた
translation: I'm sorry. / A neighbor lady told me.

vocabulary.meaning: I was wrong, I'm sorry (casual past-tense apology)

text: 須貝の鳥はどっちかが死んでしまうと / 残った一羽は後を追うように死んでしまうって / 本当にそうなった
translation: When one of a pair of lovebirds dies, / the one left behind dies as if following after. / That's exactly what happened.

vocabulary.meaning: lovebirds (lit. 'Sugai birds'; a type of paired birds said to die together)
one of the two, whichever one
to remain, to be left behind
to follow after; to follow someone in death
as if, in the manner of

grammar: 後を追うように死んでしまう — 〜ように modifies the manner of dying: 'died as if following behind.' A deeply sad image: Tidus's mother's death following Jecht's disappearance.
